headline: US Weekly Jobless Claims Reach 57-Year Low
summary: US weekly jobless claims have fallen to their lowest level in 57 years, reflecting a period of historically low layoffs in the labor market.
why: Jobless claims are a key high-frequency indicator of labor market health, which influences Federal Reserve monetary policy and broader economic growth expectations.

impacts.name: United States
impacts.why: Low jobless claims indicate a tight labor market, which can support economic growth but may also influence interest rate expectations.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Strong labor market data often fuels expectations of a resilient economy, which can lead to higher Treasury yields and potentially influence equity market sentiment.
